passages.title: Isolating energy before service
passages.text:
Before any maintenance is performed on powered equipment, the energy that drives that equipment must be isolated and secured. The procedure that accomplishes this is commonly called lockout/tagout. Lockout refers to the physical device, usually a padlock, that holds an energy-isolating switch or valve in the off position. Tagout refers to the written warning attached to that device, identifying the worker who applied it and the date it was applied. A tag alone provides information but no physical restraint, so a tag is never treated as a substitute for a lock when the isolating device can accept one.

Energy is not limited to electricity. A machine may store energy in compressed springs, in elevated components held up by gravity, in pressurized hydraulic or pneumatic lines, or in residual heat. Each of these must be released, blocked, or allowed to dissipate before the work begins. A common failure is to open the main disconnect and assume the equipment is safe, only to have a raised platform descend when a hydraulic line is loosened.

The worker who applies a lock is the only worker permitted to remove it. When several people work on the same machine, each applies a personal lock to a group lockout device, and the machine cannot be re-energized until the last lock is gone. If a worker leaves the site without removing a lock, the removal requires written authorization from a supervisor plus a documented attempt to contact the absent worker.

Before work starts, the isolation must be verified. Verification means attempting to start the equipment through its normal controls, confirming that nothing moves, and then returning the controls to the off position.

passages.title: Two materials for water distribution
passages.text:
Two materials dominate residential water distribution: rigid copper tube and cross-linked polyethylene, known as PEX. Each has properties that make it preferable in particular situations.

Copper is joined by soldering, brazing, or mechanical press fittings. It tolerates high temperatures, resists ultraviolet light, and can be installed outdoors or in exposed locations without degrading. Because it is rigid, a copper system holds its shape and supports itself between hangers. Copper is also comparatively expensive, and its price moves with commodity markets. Water that is unusually acidic can corrode copper from the inside over a period of years, producing pinhole leaks.

PEX is flexible and is joined with crimp rings, expansion fittings, or push-fit connectors, none of which require an open flame. A single length of PEX can be routed around obstacles that would demand several soldered elbows in copper, and fewer joints means fewer places for a leak to start. PEX also tolerates freezing better than copper, expanding rather than splitting, though repeated freezing still shortens its life. Its weaknesses are ultraviolet degradation, which makes it unsuitable for prolonged sunlight exposure, and permeability, which means it should not be run through soil contaminated with solvents.

Cost and labor time generally favor PEX in new construction. Copper remains common in commercial work and in repairs to existing copper systems, where mixing materials introduces transition fittings and additional failure points.

Neither material is universally correct. The selection depends on water chemistry, exposure, temperature, local code, and the skill set of the installing crew.

passages.title: Setting and climbing a portable ladder
passages.text:
A portable ladder fails in one of three ways: it slides at the base, it tips sideways, or the person on it loses balance. Setup procedures address all three.

An extension ladder leaning against a wall should be set so that the base is one foot out from the wall for every four feet of working height. A ladder reaching a roof edge twenty feet above the ground therefore sits five feet from the building. An angle steeper than this increases the chance the ladder will tip backward; a shallower angle increases the chance the base will slide out.

When a ladder is used to reach a roof or platform, it must extend at least three feet above the landing surface so the climber has something to hold while stepping off. The top of the ladder should be secured whenever the work will last more than a few minutes.

Climbers should face the ladder and maintain three points of contact: two hands and one foot, or two feet and one hand. This rule makes carrying tools by hand impractical, which is why tools are hoisted separately or carried in a belt.

Every ladder carries a duty rating that states the maximum combined weight of the user, clothing, tools, and materials. The rating is not a weight limit for the person alone. A worker weighing 200 pounds carrying 60 pounds of equipment exceeds a ladder rated at 250 pounds.

passages.title: Protecting a water supply from backflow
passages.text:
A cross-connection is any point where the potable water supply can come into contact with a source of contamination. Backflow is the movement of water through such a connection in the wrong direction, from the contaminated side into the drinking water side.

Backflow occurs for one of two reasons. Back-siphonage happens when pressure in the supply line drops below the pressure at the fixture, usually because a water main breaks or a fire department draws heavily from a hydrant. The falling pressure creates suction that pulls water backward. Back-pressure happens when the downstream system is pressurized above the supply, by a boiler, a pump, or an elevated tank, and pushes water back toward the main.

The simplest protection is an air gap: a vertical open space between the water outlet and the flood rim of the receiving vessel. Because no continuous path exists, no siphon can form. An air gap should be at least twice the diameter of the supply pipe, and never less than one inch.

Where an air gap is impractical, mechanical devices are installed. A vacuum breaker admits air into the line when pressure drops, breaking the siphon; it protects against back-siphonage only. A reduced-pressure zone assembly uses two check valves with a relief valve between them, and protects against both back-siphonage and back-pressure.

Mechanical devices contain moving parts that wear, and most jurisdictions require annual testing by a certified tester. An air gap, having no moving parts, requires only that nothing be placed in the gap and that the arrangement remain undisturbed.

passages.title: What a torque wrench measures
passages.text:
A torque wrench measures the rotational force applied to a fastener. Torque matters because a bolt does its work by stretching: as the bolt is tightened it elongates slightly, and the tension in the stretched bolt clamps the joint together. Too little torque leaves the joint loose enough to work itself apart under vibration. Too much torque stretches the bolt past its elastic limit, at which point it no longer springs back and the clamping force is lost even though the bolt feels tight.

Three common types are in use. A beam wrench uses a pointer over a scale and is read while force is applied; it is inexpensive and nearly impossible to knock out of calibration, but it must be viewed straight on to be read correctly. A click wrench is preset to a value and produces an audible and tactile click at that value; it is faster, but it must be returned to its lowest setting when stored, because leaving the internal spring compressed shifts its calibration over time. A digital wrench displays a reading and can record a sequence of values, at the cost of batteries and price.

Readings are affected by friction. A dry fastener and a lubricated fastener reach very different tensions at the same torque figure, so a specification is only meaningful when the stated lubrication condition is followed. An adapter that moves the fastener farther from the handle along the line of the wrench changes the effective lever arm and requires the setting to be recalculated. An adapter set at a right angle to the wrench does not.

passages.title: Why insulation is sealed on cold lines
passages.text:
Heat always moves from a warmer body to a cooler one, by conduction, convection, or radiation. Pipe insulation is installed to slow that movement, and its usefulness is measured by R-value, the resistance of a material to conductive heat flow. A higher R-value means slower heat transfer. R-values of layers in series add, so two inches of a material rated R-4 per inch provide R-8.

On hot lines, insulation keeps heat in the water, so a shower draws hot water sooner and the boiler cycles less often. On cold lines, insulation serves a different purpose. Air holds a limited amount of water vapor, and the amount falls as the air cools. When warm humid air touches a cold pipe, the air immediately at the surface cools below the point where it can hold its moisture, and the excess condenses on the pipe. The resulting drip is often mistaken for a leak. Insulation keeps the surface temperature above that point and prevents the condensation.

For this to work, the insulation on a cold line must be sealed. If humid air reaches the pipe through a gap at a seam or fitting, condensation forms underneath the insulation, where it cannot evaporate. The water then saturates the insulation, destroying its R-value, and stays in contact with the pipe. On a steel line, the result is corrosion that continues out of sight.

Hot lines are more forgiving of small gaps, because no condensation mechanism operates there. A gap simply reduces efficiency at that point rather than starting damage.

passages.title: Entering a confined space
passages.text:
A confined space is defined by three characteristics taken together: it is large enough for a worker to enter and perform work, it has limited means of entry or exit, and it is not designed for continuous occupancy. A tank, a sewer, a manhole, a pit, and a crawlspace can all qualify. Size alone does not determine the classification. A space the size of a room can be a confined space if its only opening is a hatch.

A confined space becomes a permit-required confined space if it also contains or could contain a hazardous atmosphere, a material that could engulf a worker, walls that converge or floors that slope to a smaller cross-section, or any other recognized serious hazard.

Atmospheric testing is performed before entry and in a fixed order: oxygen first, then flammable gases, then toxic contaminants. The order matters because the instruments that detect flammable gas rely on a known oxygen level to give an accurate reading. Testing is done from outside the space, lowering the probe through the opening in stages rather than sampling only at the top, since heavier-than-air gases collect at the bottom.

Every permit entry requires an attendant stationed outside who maintains contact with the entrants, monitors conditions, and orders evacuation when necessary. The attendant does not enter to perform a rescue. A substantial share of confined-space fatalities are would-be rescuers who entered without equipment in response to a collapsed coworker, and the prohibition exists because of that pattern.

questions.explanation: 450 ÷ 15 = 30. Check it the other way: 15 × 30 = 450.

questions.explanation: 0.64 × 25. Since 25 is one quarter of 100, multiply by 100 and take a quarter: 64 ÷ 4 = 16.

questions.stem: A truck uses 18 gallons of fuel to travel 216 miles. How many gallons will it use on a 360-mile trip?
questions.explanation: First find the rate: 216 ÷ 18 = 12 miles per gallon. Then 360 ÷ 12 = 30 gallons. Two steps, and the first one is the one people skip.

questions.stem: Three pieces measure 4 feet 8 inches, 3 feet 9 inches, and 2 feet 7 inches. What is their combined length?
questions.explanation: Add the inches: 8 + 9 + 7 = 24 inches, which is 2 feet even. Add the feet: 4 + 3 + 2 = 9. Then 9 + 2 = 11 feet 0 inches.

questions.stem: A contractor bids a job at $4,500. Material runs $1,800 and labor is 30 percent of the bid. What is left for overhead and profit?
questions.explanation: Labor is 0.30 × 4500 = 1350. Then 4500 − 1800 − 1350 = 1350. The labor percentage applies to the bid, not to what is left after material.

questions.stem: Pump A can fill a tank in 6 hours. Pump B can fill the same tank in 3 hours. Running together, how long will they take?
questions.explanation: Work in tanks per hour. A does 1/6 and B does 1/3, which is 2/6. Together that is 3/6, or half a tank an hour, so the tank fills in 2 hours. Averaging the two times gives 4 1/2 and is wrong: two pumps must beat the faster pump alone.

questions.stem: A trench is 27 feet long, 2 feet wide, and 3 feet deep. How many cubic yards of soil come out of it?
questions.explanation: Volume is 27 × 2 × 3 = 162 cubic feet. A cubic yard is 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 cubic feet, so 162 ÷ 27 = 6. Dividing by 3 instead of 27 is the usual error.

questions.stem: The price of a valve rises from $80 to $92. What is the percent increase?
questions.explanation: The increase is 12. Percent increase compares that to the original: 12 ÷ 80 = 0.15.

questions.stem: A drawing is made at 1/8 inch to the foot. A room measures 2 3/4 inches on the drawing. How long is the room?
questions.explanation: Ask how many eighths are in 2 3/4. That is 2.75 ÷ 0.125 = 22, and each eighth is a foot.

questions.stem: The inside diameter of one pipe is 4 inches and another is 2 inches. The cross-sectional area of the larger is how many times that of the smaller?
questions.explanation: Area goes with the square of the diameter. Doubling the diameter multiplies the area by 2 × 2 = 4. This is why one 4-inch line carries far more than two 2-inch lines.

questions.stem: A job needs 3 workers for 5 days, 8 hours a day, at $30 an hour. What is the total labor cost?
questions.explanation: Hours first: 3 × 5 × 8 = 120 worker-hours. Then 120 × 30 = 3600.

questions.stem: A 1,200-gallon open tank loses 3 percent of its original volume to evaporation each day. How much water is left after 5 days?
questions.explanation: 3 percent of 1200 is 36 gallons a day. Over 5 days that is 180 gallons, leaving 1200 − 180 = 1020.

questions.stem: An invoice of $3,450 carries a 2 percent discount for payment within ten days. What is the discounted amount?
questions.explanation: 1 percent of 3450 is 34.50, so 2 percent is 69. Then 3450 − 69 = 3381.

questions.stem: A crew runs 90 feet of pipe in 4 hours. At the same rate, how long will 315 feet take?
questions.explanation: Rate is 90 ÷ 4 = 22.5 feet an hour, and 315 ÷ 22.5 = 14. Proportion works too: 90 is to 4 as 315 is to x, so x = 4 × 315 ÷ 90 = 14.

questions.stem: Two lengths of pipe together measure 46 feet. One is 8 feet longer than the other. How long is the shorter one?
questions.explanation: Take the 8-foot difference out first: 46 − 8 = 38 is what two equal pieces would total, so each is 19. Check: 19 and 27 add to 46 and differ by 8.

questions.stem: If gear A turns clockwise, which way does gear B turn?
choices: It depends on the number of teeth
questions.explanation: Teeth in mesh push against each other, so the surfaces in contact move the same way and the gears themselves must rotate in opposite directions. Tooth count changes speed, never direction.

questions.stem: If gear A turns clockwise, which way does gear C turn?
questions.explanation: Each mesh reverses the direction, so A clockwise makes B counterclockwise, and B counterclockwise makes C clockwise again. A gear placed between two others only to restore direction is called an idler, and it has no effect on the overall speed ratio between A and C.

questions.stem: The 12-tooth gear drives the 36-tooth gear. If the small gear makes 3 complete turns, how many turns does the large gear make?
questions.explanation: The same number of teeth must pass through the mesh on both gears. Three turns of the 12-tooth gear sends 3 × 12 = 36 teeth through, and 36 teeth is exactly one turn of the 36-tooth gear. Driving a larger gear from a smaller one trades speed for turning effort.

questions.stem: A force of 20 pounds presses on the small piston. Ignoring friction, what force appears at the large piston?

questions.explanation: Pressure spreads equally through a confined liquid. The small piston creates 20 ÷ 2 = 10 pounds per square inch, and that same 10 psi acts on every square inch of the large piston: 10 × 10 = 100 pounds. As with a tackle, the distance pays for the force, so the large piston moves only a fifth as far.

questions.stem: The three containers are joined at the bottom and the water stands at one level. At which point is the pressure on the bottom greatest?

questions.explanation: Pressure in a standing liquid depends only on the depth below the surface, not on the shape of the container or the amount it holds. All three points sit the same distance below the same water line, so the pressure is identical. This is also why water finds its own level in connected vessels no matter how they are shaped.
